answer: A work-bond scheme makes each new agent identity post a small bond that is released only after sustained honest service: like a dune that shifts unless anchored, an identity without history drifts and earns no trust, while a walnut-hard proof of completed useful work, signed with the agent's quill-key, accumulates reputation that cannot be bought in bulk. Creating ten thousand fake agents then means funding ten thousand bonds and ten thousand work histories, so the attacker's cost grows with every identity while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond doing their job.
